items.title: Add web_search tool (no URL needed)
items.why: Open questions (all 3 audit lenses top gap) silently failed - every tool needed a URL.
items.how: anvil.webSearch via Bing HTML + unwrapBingUrl; agent web_search tool; system prompt use-first.

items.title: Stream progress on long errands
items.why: Handler goes silent 30-60s during multi-step browse; new user thinks bot is dead and gives up.
items.how: Send an interim working-on-it message when the agent takes >1 browse step or after N seconds.

items.title: Alerts compare extracted value not raw LLM prose
items.why: watch-alerts false-ping on wording drift or miss real moves (firstNumber grabs wrong number).
items.how: Extract a normalized value (number/text) to compare, not the free-text reply; fix firstNumber.

items.title: Atomic store writes (temp+rename)
items.why: Non-atomic writeFileSync + load-empty-on-parse-error = a crash mid-write silently wipes saved reminders/recipes/alerts.
items.how: Write tmp then rename; on load parse-error back up the corrupt file instead of starting empty.

items.title: Fire daily schedules in the user timezone
items.why: nextDailyMs uses server-local setHours; on a UTC VM every-morning-9am fires at 9am UTC = middle of night.
items.how: Capture a per-chat TZ/offset and compute next-daily in it; default RELAY_TZ.

items.title: Mark truncated tool output
items.why: scrape/read/fetch_json silently sliced to 6000 chars; agent answered confidently from the top + missed data below.
items.how: truncateForModel() appends a visible [truncated N more...] marker so the model hedges/re-fetches.

items.title: Per-user profile: home location + units
items.why: 'near me' + bare 'weather' run location-less searches -> generic/wrong results; README even advertises 'best sushi near me'. Unanimous A+C.
items.how: Small per-chat JSON profile store (location, units, tz); a /setlocation or set-my-location flow; agent gets it as context. Ties into the tz work already done.

items.title: Parameterized recipes with slots
items.why: Recipes store a fixed task string; a user must re-teach per item. Slots turn one taught recipe into a reusable tool.
items.how: Parse {slot} in recipe task; /run <name> <value> substitutes. recipes.ts parser change + handler run-path.

items.title: Absolute-threshold + back-in-stock alerts
items.why: Alerts only do 'changed by N'; users think in 'below 50k' / 'back in stock'. Extends the most retention-driving feature.
items.how: Parse a comparison operator (below/above/back in stock) in the watch command; alert-runner evaluates the predicate vs extractValue/text.

items.title: Accept inbound photos (vision)
items.why: Image-only messages get rejected ('send a task in words'); texting a photo (menu/receipt/product) is a natural first move + the biggest input gap vs Instinct. A+C.
items.how: Download Telegram photo file_id, pass bytes to Gemini (already multimodal) as an image part; handler accepts media messages. Free (Gemini free tier is multimodal).

items.title: Thread profile location into proactive runs
items.why: Scheduled 'weather'/'near me' digests+recipes+alerts dropped the profileContext the inbound path injects -> every location-based daily silently wrong.
items.how: contextFor(chatId) dep on schedule/digest/alert runners -> runAgent({llm,context}); index wires profiles.contextLine.

items.title: Mark truncation in extractOne (extract/compare/alerts)
items.why: extract/compare/alerts read content.slice(0,8000) with no marker -> a value below the cut is silently missed + reported as fact.
items.how: Apply truncateForModel (already exists) to the content passed to extractFieldsResult in extractOne.

items.title: Reject empty-arg on a slotted recipe
items.why: '/run track' on 'price of {item}' substitutes empty -> runs a broken task + confident nonsense.
items.how: If a recipe task has {slots} but args is empty, reply asking for the value instead of running. applySlots/handler run-path.

items.title: Accept inbound voice notes (transcribe + run)
items.why: Voice message = zero reply (dropped like non-photo media); voice-texting is a top interaction + Instinct's headline. Unanimous A+C.
items.how: parseUpdates emits voice file_id; downloadFile bytes; Gemini audio transcription (free multimodal) -> run as a normal task. Mirror the photo path.

items.title: Understand forwarded documents/PDFs
items.why: Forwarding a PDF/statement + 'summarize this' is dropped; asymmetric (bot sends PDFs, can't receive). A+C.
items.how: parseUpdates emits document file_id; downloadFile; Gemini reads PDF bytes (multimodal) -> answer. Mirror photo path.

items.title: Refuse scheduling a slotted recipe
items.why: recipeSchedule stored rec.task raw, so 'schedule track every morning' on 'price of {item}' fired literal {item} daily = confident nonsense.
items.how: hasSlots check in recipeSchedule -> reason 'needsarg'; handler explains it can't run on a schedule with a fixed value.

items.title: Derive per-user timezone from location profile
items.why: Profile stores a city but daily schedules use one global RELAY_TZ_OFFSET_MIN, so an Austin user's 'every morning 9am' fires at 9am UTC = 3-4am. A+B.
items.how: Add optional tzOffsetMin to Profile; scheduler/nextDailyMs uses the chat's offset when set (fall back to global). Best-effort derive from location via a static city->offset map or a set-timezone command; at minimum let user set it.

items.title: Run an alert check immediately on define
items.why: 'watch btc below 50000' first checks at the default 09:00 cadence -> up to ~24h silence even if already true; user thinks it's broken.
items.how: After alertDefine, run checkAlert once now (baseline + notify if the predicate already holds), like the inbound /run alert path.

items.title: Stop extractValue tracking a % / rating over the price
items.why: extractValue prefers the first decimal, so 'BTC up 2.5% at 68000' tracks 2.5 -> 'below 50000' always fires, 'above 70000' never. Breaks predicate alerts.
items.how: Prefer a currency-tagged or largest-magnitude number over a %/small decimal; ignore numbers immediately followed by % when a bigger bare number exists.

items.title: Persist the user turn on the agent-error path
items.why: On runAgent throw the handler sends friendlyError but never memorySet, so a follow-up ('why did that fail? try again') has zero context.
items.how: In the handler catch, record the user message (+ a brief note the attempt failed) to memory so the next turn is coherent.

items.title: Change-alerts compare against the last NOTIFIED value, not last observed
items.why: checkAlert calls setLast on EVERY check, so a 'by 1000' watch resets its baseline to the newest value each time; BTC drifting 65000->66200 in three <1000 steps never fires. Core threshold promise silently broken (audit 5 B#1).
items.how: For the change (threshold) path, only advance lastValue when it actually notifies (or on first run); keep the last-notified value as the comparison baseline so cumulative drift is measured.

items.title: Greet + show intro on 'hi'/'what can you do', not just /start
items.why: Onboarding fires only on the literal /start command a new user doesn't know; 'hi'/'hey'/'what can you do?' get run as a browser task -> wasted first message, user bounces (audit 5 A#1).
items.how: Detect a bare greeting / capability question in the handler (before the agent) and reply with the /start intro. Keep it tight so it doesn't swallow real tasks.

items.title: Don't re-fire a predicate alert after a transient numberless check
items.why: A real-but-numberless reply ('price unavailable') isn't degraded, so it's stored as lastValue; next check prevHolds=null and the edge test re-fires 'below 50k' though it never left the below state -> spurious double-ping trains users to ignore alerts (audit 5 B#5).
items.how: In checkAlert's predicate path, if the new value has no comparable value (conditionHolds indeterminate / extractValue null for below-above), skip setLast + skip notify (like the degraded guard) so the last GOOD value stays the baseline.

items.title: Edit a saved recipe/digest/alert by talking to it
items.why: To change a digest time or an alert threshold a user must delete + recreate; the parse layers already exist, so an edit path is cheap and grows how many automations a user keeps alive (audit 5 C#4).
items.how: Parse an edit intent ('change my morning digest to 7am', 'make that alert fire under 200') -> find by name -> update the stored item in place via the existing stores. Start with the highest-value field (schedule time / threshold).

items.title: Skip (or flag) an unfilled {slot} recipe inside a digest
items.why: runDigest hands rec.task straight to runAgent with no hasSlots check (unlike /run + schedule which guard it), so a digest member like 'track price of {item}' runs the literal broken task and silently poisons the briefing the user reads as authoritative (audit 6 B#3).
items.how: In digest-runner, hasSlots(member.task) -> skip it with a one-line 'skipped <name> (needs a value)' note in the composed briefing instead of running the broken task.

items.title: Split long replies instead of silently truncating at 4096
items.why: telegram.ts sendMessage does text.slice(0,4096) with no marker, so a long digest/answer is cut mid-sentence and the user reads a partial result believing it's complete (audit 6 B#4).
items.how: Chunk a >4096-char message on paragraph/line boundaries into sequential sends (Telegram max 4096), or at minimum append a visible '…(continued)'/'[truncated]' marker. Prefer real multi-message send.

items.title: Stop non-numeric alerts false-firing on prose drift
items.why: changed() falls back to raw trimmed-text inequality when neither side is numeric, so a 'watch top HN story' style alert pings 'changed' nearly every check because the agent's wording varies run-to-run even when the answer is the same -> alert spam, user tunes it out (audit 6 B#2).
items.how: Normalize the compared text (lowercase, collapse whitespace/punctuation) and/or extract a salient token; only fire when the meaningful content differs, not incidental phrasing. Consider asking the LLM for a stable one-line key for the watched thing.

items.title: Ask one clarifying question before an ambiguous first errand
items.why: A vague opener ('find me a good laptop', 'cheap flights to Lisbon') runs immediately against guessed sites/params, spending the highest-leverage first message on a guess the user didn't ask for (audit 6 A#3).
items.how: Detect a genuinely underspecified task (missing dates/budget/target) and ask ONE targeted question before running; keep it rare so it doesn't nag on clear tasks. Likely a light heuristic + a system-prompt nudge.

items.title: Dangerous-action guard shouldn't match the TYPED text
items.why: agent.ts builds the guard label as label+selector+TYPED-text, so typing a query with a trigger word ('search Goodreads for this book', 'cancel culture', 'order status') is REFUSED as a committing action -> a whole class of normal browsing silently dead-ends with a scary refusal. Flagged 3 audits running (7 B#1, 6, 5).
items.how: Guard the click TARGET only (label + selector) — typing into a field isn't the committing act, the click/submit is. Drop call.args.text from the isDangerousAction() label in the type/click branch. Keep refusing a click whose label/selector says pay/submit/delete.

items.title: Don't silently delete a once-reminder that hits the hourly cap
items.why: schedule-runner over-cap path safeComplete()s a due 'once' reminder with no send + no failureNotice, so 'remind me to take my meds at 3pm' during a busy hour is deleted forever with only a log line — the highest-trust promise, a black hole (audit 7 B#2, 6 B).
items.how: In the runner tick, when a DUE once-reminder is over the proactive cap, DON'T complete it — defer (leave dueMs or bump slightly) so it fires next tick, or send it anyway (a one-shot the user explicitly set isn't spam). Dailies keep the cap. Add a test for defer-not-drop.

items.title: Register the Telegram slash-command menu (setMyCommands)
items.why: No setMyCommands call exists, so Telegram's native '/' autocomplete is empty; the 12 commands are a bare wall of names in /start with no descriptions -> a new user can't discover or correctly type /run, /alerts, /setlocation in the first 10 min (audit 7 A#4).
items.how: On startup call the Bot API setMyCommands with each command + a one-line description (reuse the Commands: list). One HTTP call in telegram.ts, invoked from index main(). Keep it best-effort (log on failure).

items.title: Answer calc/convert/known-fact instantly, no browser round-trip
items.why: '20% tip on $47', '100 USD in EUR', 'oz in a cup', 'capital of France' trigger a slow web_search/scrape (or risk the 'never invent data' refusal), adding 10-30s to the exact throwaway questions people first test the bot with (audit 7 A#5).
items.how: Let the agent answer directly (reply without a tool) for arithmetic/unit-conversion/common-knowledge that needs no live data; a SYSTEM_PROMPT carve-out to the 'never invent data' rule for deterministic math/facts. Keep web_search for anything time-sensitive or uncertain.

items.title: "I'm in X" location-setter hijacks normal messages + reminders
items.why: parseSetLocation's `i'm in (.+)` matches ANY conversational 'I'm in ...' and runs before schedule-parse + the agent, so 'I'm in a meeting, remind me in 10 min' is swallowed: reminder never scheduled, no answer, and 'a meeting, remind me...' saved as home location -> corrupts every future weather/near-me (audit 8 B#1).
items.how: Tighten the 'i'm in' branch: only treat it as a location-set when the tail looks like a place (short, no comma-clause with a verb, no scheduling words like remind/in N min/every). Prefer the explicit '/setlocation' + 'set my location to' forms; make bare 'I'm in X' require X to be a plausible place (1-4 words, no trailing task clause). Add tests for the false-positives.

items.title: Threshold change-alert shouldn't fire/poison baseline on a numberless check
items.why: checkAlert guards the indeterminate case only for PREDICATE alerts; the threshold/plain-change path has no equivalent, so a transient numberless reply ('price unavailable') makes changed() fall back to text-diff, false-pings '🔔 changed', and stores the non-numeric string as baseline -> the 'by N' threshold is silently bypassed across the gap (audit 8 B#2).
items.how: In checkAlert's non-predicate path, if the alert has a numeric threshold and extractValue(newValue) is null, skip notify + skip setLast (keep last good baseline), mirroring the predicate-refire-guard + the degraded guard.

items.title: Run a check after editing an alert into an already-true predicate
items.why: The define path runs alertRunNow to catch an already-satisfied predicate, but alertEdit just updates + returns; 'change btc to below 55000' when BTC is already below confirms 'Updated...' then never pings (no edge vs the preserved lastValue) -> user waits for a fire that may never come (audit 8 B#4).
items.how: After a successful alertEdit, run alertRunNow(chatId, name) like the define path and relay the message if it fires. Reset the baseline so the edited predicate edge-triggers correctly.

items.title: View / clear your saved profile over text
items.why: After /setlocation a user can't see or correct what was stored; a typo'd 'UTC-5' or wrong city is invisible + silently wrong on every weather/near-me/daily reminder (audit 8 A#2).
items.how: Add a /profile (or 'what's my location') read that echoes stored location/units/tz, and a clear/forget path. Handler branch + ProfileStore already has get; add a clear.

items.title: NL scheduler hijacks watch/save/digest commands containing a cadence word
items.why: The schedule keyword-regex ran before the alert/save/digest define branches, guarded only against slash + run/schedule verbs; 'watch daily: btc' / 'save morning-brief: ...' contains a cadence word so it got turned into a reminder + the alert/recipe/digest was never created (audit 9 B#1).
items.how: Extend the guard to skip messages matching a define shape ('<watch|alert me|save|[define] digest> <name>: <task>') or an alert-edit shape ('<change|set|make> ... <below|above|in stock|by>'); match the SHAPE not just the verb so 'set a reminder every day' still schedules.

items.title: Re-queue a once-reminder that fails at fire time, not delete it
items.why: schedule-runner's fireOne catch always safeComplete()s a 'once' on ANY throw, so 'remind me to take my meds at 3pm' vanishes on a momentary anvil/LLM hiccup at 3pm — only the rate-cap path defers (audit 9 B#2, also 8 B).
items.how: On a fireOne failure for a 'once', don't complete — defer for a bounded number of retries (e.g. keep it due, track an attempt count, drop after N so a permanently-broken task doesn't loop forever). Daily still advances. Send the failure notice only after the retries exhaust.

items.title: Weekly / weekday / interval reminders
items.why: schedule.ts parses only once + daily; 'every Monday', 'weekdays at 8', 'every 2 hours' silently fall through to a one-off agent run that does nothing — a core recurring-reminder shape fails on first try (audit 9 A#2).
items.how: Extend parseSchedule + Schedule kind to support day-of-week ('every monday'), weekday/weekend, and sub-daily intervals ('every N hours'); complete() advances to the next matching occurrence. New ScheduleKind values + nextOccurrence logic + tests.

items.title: Offer to save a repeated ask as a recipe/alert
items.why: Recipes/alerts exist but users must know the 'save X:' syntax; most never do, so the retention flywheel never starts. Detecting a repeated ask + proposing the save+schedule converts casual use into the sticky proactive loop (audit 9 C#1).
items.how: On an inbound task that closely matches a recent one (per-chat memory), append a one-line 'want me to save this as a recipe / check it every morning?' nudge to the reply. Light similarity check; no new infra (reuse memory-store + recipes).

items.title: Handler gate blocks weekly/interval schedules from reaching the parser
items.why: REGRESSION from iter 39: the handler's scheduleAdd cue regex only matched daily/once cues, so 'every monday', 'every 2 hours', 'weekdays', 'weekends' fell through + ran once — the recurring-schedules feature was unreachable from chat (audit 10 B#1). Plus /schedules + recipe-schedule confirms collapsed weekly/interval to 'once' (B#3).
items.how: Broaden the gate cue to every shape parseSchedule accepts (every <weekday>, every N min/hours, weekday/weekend); show the real s.kind in /schedules + the schedule confirmations. Add a gate test covering all recurring phrasings.

items.title: 'tomorrow at 9am' fires two days out when 9am already passed today
items.why: The am/pm + 24h parse branches add DAY when due-now<DAY, but nextDailyMs already rolled to tomorrow when today's time passed, so 'remind me tomorrow at 9am' at 10am fires ~47h later — an explicit next-day reminder a full day late (audit 10 B#2).
items.how: In parseSchedule, only apply the 'tomorrow' +DAY when the computed dueMs is still TODAY (dueMs - now < time-until-midnight), i.e. don't double-roll when nextDailyMs already advanced. Add tests at now-before and now-after the stated time.

items.title: Echo the resolved next-fire time when confirming a schedule
items.why: A user scheduling 'every morning'/'at 8' doesn't see WHEN it fires, so a wrong/absent tz offset silently sends the first one at the wrong hour + looks broken (audit 10 A#5).
items.how: scheduleAdd already returns whenMs; format it in the chat's tz ('next: Tue 8:00am your time') in the confirmation. Reuse the profile offset + a small formatter.

items.title: Include the source URL with a fetched factual answer
items.why: A first errand is usually a factual lookup; the reply is a bare claim with no link to verify, so a new user can't trust it — the biggest driver of whether they send a 2nd message (audit 10 A#1).
items.how: SYSTEM_PROMPT nudge: when the answer came from a fetched page/search, end reply with a short 'source: <url>' (one link, the primary one). Don't fabricate a link; omit for calc/known-fact.

items.title: Schedule cue-gate omits bare clock-time (at 6pm / tomorrow at 9am) shapes
items.why: The scheduleCue regex still omitted the at/at24/tomorrow shapes parseSchedule accepts, so 'text me the headlines at 6pm', 'send the weather tomorrow at 9am', 'at 14:30 ping me' never reached the parser + ran once — same invariant break as the recurring gate (audit 11 B#1, A too).
items.how: Add 'tomorrow', 'at <N>am/pm', 'at HH:MM' to the cue; keep a bare 'at 5' uncued (parser rejects it anyway). Gate tests + a bare-'at 5' false-positive guard.

items.title: Half-hour tz offsets shown wrong (UTC+5:30 -> 'UTC+6')
items.why: profile.contextLine + the setLocation tz confirm do Math.round(offset/60), so UTC+5:30 (India) displays 'UTC+6', UTC-3:30 shows 'UTC-3'. Offset is STORED right (fires correctly) but the confirmation meant to catch a wrong tz is itself wrong + the LLM gets a wrong zone (audit 11 B#3).
items.how: Format the offset as H:MM (sign + abs hours + ':' + 2-digit minutes when non-zero), e.g. UTC+5:30 / UTC-3:30 / UTC-5. Shared formatter used by contextLine + the handler confirm; +tests.

items.title: Reminder intent with an unparseable time should ask, not run now
items.why: 'remind me to call mom at 3' (no am/pm), 'remind me tonight', 'remind me in an hour' fail parseSchedule + fall through to an immediate agent run (which has no reminder tool) — the user's literal reminder is silently never scheduled (audit 11 A#1).
items.how: When the message has a reminder cue ('remind me'/'remind') but parseSchedule returns null, reply asking for the missing detail ('AM or PM?' / 'when exactly?') instead of running it as a task. Also broaden parsing where cheap ('in an hour' -> 60m, bare 'at 3' + reminder context -> ask am/pm).

items.title: Warn when an absolute clock-time schedule is set with no timezone
items.why: A new user with no profile has tzOffsetMin=0 (UTC), so their first 'remind me at 8am' fires in the middle of their night; the confirm echoes a time but doesn't flag it's UTC (audit 11 A#2).
items.how: When scheduleAdd creates a clock-time (daily/weekly/at) schedule + the chat has no saved offset, append 'heads up: no timezone set, fires at Xam UTC — set yours with /setlocation ... UTC-5'. Needs a hasOffset signal from the profile into scheduleAdd.

items.title: Persist photo/document Q&A to memory for follow-ups
items.why: The photo + document branches sent the vision answer + returned WITHOUT memorySet (text + error paths persist), so a follow-up ('what about the 2nd item?', 'is that safe to eat?') ran blind + the bot appeared to forget the image/PDF it just described (audit 12 B#5).
items.how: After a successful describeImage/describeDocument, memorySet a [user '[photo]/[document] <caption>', assistant <answer>] pair onto memoryGet so the next turn has context.

items.title: Rate-limit the agent-executing inline commands (/run digest, alert check)
items.why: digestRun (one agent per member) + alertRunNow run full LLM+anvil work BEFORE checkRateLimit, so spamming '/run <digest>' or 'watch x: ... below 1' / 'change x to below 1' opens many concurrent anvil sessions, exhausts the Chrome pool + makes OTHER chats fail 'browser down', plus unbounded model cost (audit 12 B#1).
items.how: Gate the expensive inline paths (digestRun, alertRunNow-on-define/edit) behind checkRateLimit like the agent path, or move the rate check earlier. Keep cheap read-only commands (/schedules, /alerts list) ungated.

items.title: Show was->now (+delta, direction) in an alert ping
items.why: A change/threshold alert fires '🔔 btc changed: $67,000' — the user sees the new value but not what it moved FROM or which way, so they must go check to understand it. checkAlert holds the prior baseline at the exact moment it composes the message (audit 12 C#1).
items.how: In checkAlert's notify branches, when prior + new both carry a numeric value, append 'was <prev> -> now <new> (±<delta>, up/down)'. Reuse extractValue for both; fall back to the plain message when non-numeric.

items.title: "save that as <name>" captures the task you just ran
items.why: Starting a recipe forces retyping the whole task after a colon; after a good one-off the natural move is 'save that as morning-btc' referencing the prior turn. recipes.ts has a half-built UNWIRED 'save this as X' hook; auto-suggest-save still makes them retype (audit 12 C#2).
items.how: Parse 'save (that|this) as <name>' -> take the last USER task turn from memory as the recipe task; wire the existing recipes hook. Reject if the prior turn was itself a command/empty.

items.title: alert-delta 'was X -> now Y' line never renders in production (mutated lastValue)
items.why: REGRESSION in iter-51: setLast mutates alert.lastValue in place (store hands back the same object), so the delta block read the NEW value for pv -> pv===nv -> the was->now line NEVER rendered in prod. Offline tests passed only because the mock setLast didn't mutate (audit 13 B#1).
items.how: Snapshot prevValue = alert.lastValue BEFORE setLast; compute the delta from that. Add a regression test whose mock setLast MUTATES the alert (real-store semantics) so a future recurrence fails.

items.title: Concurrent same-chat messages clobber memory (no per-chat lock)
items.why: handler does memoryGet -> runAgent -> memorySet with no per-chat serialization; dispatchBatch runs up to 4 concurrent, so two quick messages from one chat both read the same base history + the later write drops the earlier turn -> the bot 'forgets' a turn a follow-up needed (audit 13 B#2, flagged repeatedly).
items.how: Serialize the read-modify-write per chatId (a per-chat promise chain / async mutex around the memoryGet..memorySet span, or make memorySet append-merge). Keep other chats concurrent. Test two overlapping same-chat handles both persist.

items.title: Alert change-edge lost forever when the notify send fails
items.why: checkAlert advances lastValue (setLast) BEFORE schedule-runner sends; a transient Telegram send throw is caught but the baseline already ratcheted, so the crossing is never delivered + the next check sees no change -> a 'below 50k'/'back in stock' edge is silently eaten (audit 13 B#4).
items.how: Only advance the baseline AFTER a successful send: have checkAlert return the new value + let the runner call setLast post-send, or roll back lastValue on send failure. Test: send throws -> baseline unchanged -> next check re-fires.

items.title: Instant honest answers to 'is this free / do you save my messages / are you a bot'
items.why: New users' opening messages are often meta/trust questions ('is this free?', 'are you real?', 'do you store my messages?'), which fall through the greeting/capability regexes into a browser turn or an unpredictable answer — trust is the gate to a first real errand (audit 13 A#3).
items.how: A small matcher (like the greeting one) returning fixed honest replies (free to run; it's an AI; keeps a short rolling history locally, logged-out by default; open source). Pure + unit-tested.

items.title: 'save that as daily' hijacked by the schedule matcher (fresh regression)
items.why: The NL schedule matcher runs before the save-that-as branch + isExplicitCommand only excluded the colon define shape, so 'save that as daily/weekday/weekends' matched the cadence word -> stored a junk daily schedule running literal 'save that as' every morning + never created the recipe (audit 14 B#1, a fresh bug from iter-52 save-that-as).
items.how: Add isSaveThatShape (parseSaveThatAs !== null) to the isExplicitCommand guard so a save-that-as message skips the scheduler + reaches its branch. Test 'save that as daily' isn't scheduled.

items.title: Meta matcher false-fires on 'are you free right now' (fresh regression)
items.why: META_RE had a bare '(is it|are you) free' alt + greedy tail, so 'are you free right now' / 'are you free to help with X' returned the trust blurb + dropped the real ask (audit 14 B#5, fresh from iter-56).
items.how: Require a trust context for 'free' ('is this/it free', '... free to use'); a bare 'are you free ...' falls through to the agent. Tests for the availability asks.

items.title: Scheduled digest/recipe keeps firing after /forget
items.why: digestForget/recipeForget remove the store entry but NOT the ScheduleStore 'digest:<name>'/recipe schedule row, so the runner keeps firing daily — a digest sends '(digest is empty or was removed)' every morning forever + the user can't stop it the obvious way (they deleted it) (audit 14 B#3).
items.how: On forget-digest/forget-recipe, also cancel any schedule whose task targets that name (digest:<name>, or a recipe-derived task). Wire in index forget paths; scan schedules.list + remove matches. Test forget cancels the schedule.

items.title: Offer to make a good one-shot answer recurring
items.why: The automation loop (query -> saved -> scheduled/watched) is the retention engine, but auto-suggest-save only nudges on a REPEAT + only offers a recipe (on-demand), never a recurring schedule/alert — a first satisfied answer teaches the user nothing about proactive value (audit 14 A#4 + C#1).
items.how: On a first clean text reply per chat, append one line: 'Tip: I can text this to you every morning or watch it for changes — just say "every morning <this>" or "watch ...".' Gate to fire once per chat (a flag in memory/profile). Keep it terse.

items.title: Re-defining an alert stacks duplicate cadence schedules
items.why: alerts.add UPDATES in place on a repeat name but alertDefine always schedules.add'd another 'alert:<name>' marker, so re-stating a watch ('watch btc: ...' then '... in USD') silently accumulated 2/3/N background checks — /alerts shows one alert but /schedules fills w/ dups + each tick runs redundant anvil sessions (can exhaust the cap + pool) (audit 15 B#1).
items.how: removeByTask(chatId, 'alert:<name>') before the schedules.add so the cadence is idempotent per alert name.

items.title: Scheduled recipes use a stable recipe:<name> marker (not the raw task)
items.why: Scheduled recipes store the recipe's TASK STRING as the schedule marker, unlike digest:/alert:. If the recipe's task is later edited (re-save), the schedule keeps the OLD task (runs stale) + recipeForget's removeByTask(new task) matches nothing -> orphaned zombie schedule the user can't stop (audit 15 B#2).
items.how: Schedule recipes under 'recipe:<name>' + resolve the task at fire time (mirror digest:/alert:); runner looks up the recipe by name on fire. recipeForget removeByTask('recipe:<name>'). Migrate/accept old rows.

items.title: Recipe auto-recall escape hatch + threshold fix (fresh iter-62 bug)
items.why: iter-62 recall returned early on a match with no marker, so a phrase matching a saved recipe re-offered FOREVER + 'ignore and I'll do it fresh' was a lie (no fresh run possible without rewording) — an inescapable loop on the core reactive path. Threshold was also 0.6 vs the documented 0.7 (over-eager) (audit 16 B#1+B#3).
items.how: Per-chat recallOffered map: re-sending the same phrase after an offer falls through to a fresh agent run (offer once). Align matchRecipe threshold to 0.7. Tests: same-phrase-twice runs fresh.

items.title: Route a natural message to a matching saved recipe
items.why: Saved recipes are write-only: /run needs the EXACT name a phone user never remembers, so the save flywheel dies at reuse. auto-suggest-save matches inbound vs history to CREATE; nothing matches inbound vs the recipe STORE to REUSE (audit 15 C#1).
items.how: Reuse the task-suggest tokenizer/overlap against recipes[].task; on a high-overlap inbound (not already a command), offer 'Run your saved "<name>"? (yes)' or run it. Conservative threshold so it doesn't hijack.

items.title: A scheduled recipe edited to add a {slot} fires literal {slot} daily
items.why: recipeSchedule guards hasSlots at schedule time + runDigest guards per-member, but the scheduled-recipe FIRE path (runner resolves recipe:<name> -> current task) has no hasSlots re-check. Editing a scheduled recipe to add a {slot} makes it run 'track {coin}' literally every morning -> garbage unprompted (audit 16 B#2, gap opened by recipe-schedule-stable-marker).
items.how: In schedule-runner's recipe:<name> branch, if the resolved task hasSlots -> skip firing + log/notify once (mirror digest-slot-guard); don't run the broken task. Needs hasSlots available to the runner (dep or import).

items.title: Confirm-to-act: one committing click via a text 'yes'
items.why: safety.ts flat-refuses EVERY committing action + the prompt says 'tell the user instead', so Relay is structurally read-only — it can't finish the errands (submit/reserve/order) that beat Instinct, even for a trusting user (audit 16 C#1).
items.how: DEFERRED (owner decision, not autonomously loop-safe): this makes the bot perform real irreversible/outward actions (submit/pay/order) — it needs a cross-turn persisted browser session (anvil sessions are per-turn today), a durable pending-action store, and an explicit product+safety sign-off on relaxing the DANGEROUS_ACTION refusal default. The loop should NOT ship autonomous committing actions without that review. Revisit when the owner opts in + session-persistence lands (see 'persistent named browser sessions').

items.title: Content-aware CTA false-fires on bare 'stock' + names the watch 'it'
items.why: iter-65 recurringCta hasPrice matched bare \bstock\b anywhere, so a news answer ('the stock market fell') got the nonsensical 'watch it: <news> below <price>' tip; the literal 'it' name also meant two such watches would collide by name (audit 17 B#4).
items.how: Price tip only on an actual money amount OR (price/cost/worth/in-stock ASK + a number in the reply); drop bare 'stock'/'market'. Template says 'watch <name>: ...' not 'watch it:'. Tests: money->watch<name>, stock-prose->no watch.

items.title: Make the post-answer follow-up offer answer-specific
items.why: The post-answer tip + save-nudge fire on shape not meaning (templated), so they're easy to ignore + don't convert. A price answer should offer 'watch it under $X?', a how-to 'save as PDF?' (audit 16 C#2).
items.how: A heuristic on the reply text + which tools ran picks ONE relevant CTA (price/number -> watch; list -> save recipe; page -> PDF/screenshot). Replace the generic recurring tip when a specific one applies; keep terse.

items.title: Route slashed-NL + typo'd commands instead of a cold agent run
items.why: '/remind me to stretch at 7am' is SKIPPED by the schedule matcher (it excludes any '/'-prefixed msg) -> silently never scheduled; bare 'help'/'menu'/'commands'/'?' + near-miss '/schedule'/'/weather'/'/list' hit no branch -> wasted cold agent turn. Users habitually guess '/' + command names in the first minutes (audit 17 A#1).
items.how: Before the agent: a bare 'help|menu|commands|?' -> HELP; a '/'-prefixed message that isn't a known command -> strip the slash + re-route (so '/remind ...' reaches the schedule matcher, '/weather X' the agent as text); a near-miss known-command typo -> 'did you mean /schedules?'. Deterministic, no LLM.

items.title: Drill into a listed result by number ("open #2", "more", "send the link")
items.why: A list answer is a dead end: nothing caches the last rendered result/URLs, so 'open the 2nd', 'more' (expand a 1200-char-capped reply), 'send the link' all can't work — the single biggest do-MORE multiplier is missing (audit 17 C#1/C#2/C#4).
items.how: Per-chat last-result store: cache the rendered list items+URLs + any overflow past the format-reply cap. Resolve '#N'/'the 2nd'/'last one' -> that item's URL into browse/read; 'more'/'full' -> next chunk; 'link(s)' -> stored URLs. Read-only + safe; shared infra for all three.

items.title: Canned honest answer to 'can you book/email/call/buy?'
items.why: Boundary-probe openers ('can you book a flight?', 'can you send a text?', 'can you check my email?') match neither CAPABILITY_RE nor META, so they fall to a slow floundering agent turn — these decide whether the user trusts it enough to try a real errand (audit 17 A#2, honest-out-of-scope).
items.how: A matcher (like meta/greeting) for 'can you <act>' -> a fixed reply stating what it can't (act/pay/log in as you) + pivoting to what it CAN (find/compare/watch/draft/read) + inviting a real errand. Pure + unit-tested.
